clue.text: Duck head behind middle of pedestal

indicators.note: behind says the head-word comes after the other piece, fixing their order
the middle of a word is its central pair of letters, so only the centre of pedestal is kept

parts.note: the fourth and fifth of its eight letters
a cape is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone ducks down behind the middle of a statue's pedestal to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: Head is a geographical headland here, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a duty or a blow is to evade or get away from it, which is what escape means.

clue.text: Don't allow artists in German town to show up

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the German town

parts.note: Ems, now Bad Ems, a German spa town
to bar is to forbid
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep artists out of a German town so they do not appear.
explanation.walkthrough: Ems is the spa town known from the Ems telegram of 1870.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to make them look foolish in public, the same as causing them shame.

clue.text: Minded about the French being exonerated

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the minded word goes round the French

parts.note: to mind about something is to care
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone cared that the French were found not guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exonerated is to be declared free of blame, which is being acquitted or found innocent.

clue.text: Pretend to be an impresario

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to stage a performer's show, as a promoter does

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally for the impresario, who presents a turn on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to feign or pose, and taken literally describes a promoter presenting a performer's turn.

clue.text: Preserve, excellent preserve, from Kingston, possibly

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is written as I
to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: A jar of fine jam, sold as coming from Kingston, perhaps a market there.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word, preserve, is used once as a noun and once as a verb. Kingston is the capital of Jamaica; possibly flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing originating in Kingston would be described as Jamaican, Kingston being that island nation's capital city.

clue.text: Does it require deciphering from a GP author?

definitions.text: Does it require deciphering from a GP author?

indicators.note: deciphering means unscrambling a jumbled text, so these letters are worked into order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A joke about doctors' notoriously illegible handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a signature from a doctor, GP being a family doctor in Britain, is famously hard to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature in someone's own hand is a scrawl that, from a doctor, readers may struggle to make out.

clue.text: Half of what Robin Hood was involved in appears crooked

indicators.note: only half the word's letters are kept here, its second four, with the first four dropped

parts.words: what Robin Hood was involved in
parts.note: Robin Hood lived as an outlaw, so he was involved in outlawry, the condition of being outside the law

explanation.surface: Something about the Sherwood Forest legend seems to have gone wrong or bent.
explanation.walkthrough: The eight-letter word splits evenly, and the back half is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew or out of true is crooked, the usual synonym pairing.

clue.text: Coach — it crashes, out of control

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coach runs out of control and crashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is in total disorder, with nobody in charge, which is being out of control.

clue.text: In legend, by ignoring the odds, become poor

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters leaves only the second, fourth, sixth and so on

parts.note: the even letters of in legend by

explanation.surface: A story where a character ignores the odds and ends up penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignoring the odds sounds like defying chance, but it means leaving out the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy people lack money and basic necessities, which is what being poor means.

clue.text: Hide tear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an animal's skin with the fur on
second meaning: to rush along at speed

explanation.walkthrough: Hide and tear look like verbs of concealing and ripping; they are a skin and a dash at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for an animal's furry skin and a verb for running very fast.

clue.text: Inspire soldiers to swim around

indicators.note: around says the swimming word wraps itself about the soldiers

parts.note: to bathe is to take a swim
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A commander tries to motivate the troops to go for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspire is used in its literal sense of drawing air into the lungs, not motivating.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire in the physiological sense is to draw air in, which is breathing in.

clue.text: Sovereign occupying 19 houses in a row

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit inside something, so the sovereign goes within the other piece

parts.note: 19 across is a soupcon, a tiny amount, which is a trace
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch moves into a row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also a gold coin, but here it is the monarch. The cross-reference sends you to the answer to 19 across, whose meaning is used.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a terrace is a row of joined houses built as one continuous block along a street.

clue.text: Gung-ho gunners encircle African republic

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
to ring is to encircle
Togo is a West African republic

explanation.surface: Eager artillerymen surround an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho means wildly enthusiastic and eager for action, the same as being impatient to start.

clue.text: Delay a guy

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rope or wire bracing a mast or tent

explanation.walkthrough: Guy looks like a man, but it is the rope that holds up a tent or mast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a postponement or holding back and a supporting rope on a ship's mast.

clue.text: One way to get purchase standing on spade, perhaps

parts.note: your credit is your financial standing
a spade is one suit of playing card

explanation.surface: Advice on getting a grip by standing on a garden spade.
explanation.walkthrough: Purchase sounds like grip or foothold, but it is buying; on puts the first piece before the second in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying by plastic is one method of making a purchase, with the bank lending the money.

clue.text: Supplements showing how to make gag crazy?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: additions to a book or document

definitions.text: showing how to make gag crazy?
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: split the answer into three words; putting a letter after gag gives gaga, which means crazy

explanation.surface: Extra pages that explain how to turn a joke into madness.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words it is an instruction: put one letter on the end of gag to make gaga, slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added at the close of a book or report, so they are supplementary material.

clue.text: Strengthening girl, a swimmer

parts.note: a girl's name
taken as written
the ling is a fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: A girl swimmer is getting stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: Swimmer is a fish, a common crossword use.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing heats and slowly cools metal or glass to toughen it, a process of hardening and making it less brittle.

clue.text: Fruit and lots of cereal put in a pan

indicators.note: put in says the cereal is placed inside the container named next

parts.note: a pan is a pot, with the article kept

indicators.note: lots of is less than all, so the cereal word loses its last letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A recipe: fruit and plenty of cereal go into a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange-yellow stone fruit, so it is one example of a fruit.

clue.text: Catches fish to support some, but not others

definitions.text: to support some, but not others

parts.note: to take is to catch
the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe

explanation.surface: An angler lands some fish to feed some people but not others.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking sides in a dispute means backing one party against the rest, which is supporting only some.

clue.text: Dash! Coupons rendered invalid

indicators.note: something rendered invalid is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance: the vouchers have expired.
explanation.walkthrough: Dash! looks like a mild oath, but it is a small amount, as in a dash of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash of something is a tiny quantity, and the French-derived word for a small trace means the same.

clue.text: In old city, pruned shrub back towards source

indicators.note: in places the trimmed shrub inside the old city

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: a pruned plant has been cut back, so the shrub loses its last letter

parts.note: privet is a hedging shrub

explanation.surface: In an ancient city a gardener cuts back a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: Back reads with pruned, as in cut back, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading upriver is travelling against the current, back in the direction of where a river rises.

clue.text: Fish got cut

parts.note: had means obtained or got
to dock is to cut short, as a tail or wages

explanation.surface: A fisherman reports that a fish he caught was sliced up.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish related to the cod, a staple of British fish and chips.

clue.text: There's nothing to restrict the view

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
to pinion is to bind someone's arms, restricting them

explanation.surface: A complaint that nothing blocks the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: View looks like scenery but means a point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view in the sense of an outlook or belief is a personal judgement on a matter.

clue.text: Communist reported in German capital

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Karl Marx, the founding thinker of communism

explanation.surface: A Communist is said to be living in or holding power in Germany's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' looks like Berlin, but capital here means money: the old West German currency unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deutschmark was Germany's currency before the euro, and capital can mean money.

clue.text: Slough has army hospital right in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle says the direction letter sits inside the hospital word

parts.note: MASH, a mobile army surgical hospital
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The town of Slough contains a military hospital at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town near London, but here it is the common noun for a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or patch of soft wet ground, the same as a marsh or bog.

clue.text: Return flight is secret

parts.note: to come back is to return
a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: A homeward plane journey is being kept confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: Return flight suggests air travel, but flight is a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstairs as an adjective means underhand or clandestine, from the servants' stairs used out of sight.

clue.text: Knight is buried inside ancient tomb

indicators.note: to be buried inside something is to be enclosed by it, so is goes into the knight's abbreviation

parts.note: Kt is the abbreviation for knight
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight lies buried within an old tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: Kist is a rare word, a Scots form of chest also used for a prehistoric stone coffin, better known as a cist.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeologists use the word for a stone-lined burial box of prehistoric times, a variant spelling of cist.

clue.text: Vessel's left harbour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the left-hand side of a ship facing forward
second meaning: a place where ships dock

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ship departing a harbour; left is a direction, not a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the left-hand side of a ship and a town or haven where ships load and unload.

clue.text: Possible diet of Italian opera violinist needs

indicators.note: the words need the answer in the sense of containing it, so it sits within them

parts.note: spans the end of opera and the start of violinist

explanation.surface: A musician in an Italian opera orchestra needs a particular diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: an Italian might well eat this.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small stuffed pasta parcels, a typical food an Italian person might eat, hence possible diet.

clue.text: Jack is among hard-liners backing flier

indicators.note: to be among others is to be surrounded by them, so the sailor goes inside
backing means going backwards, so the hard-liners are read from the end

parts.note: in British politics dries were hard-line Thatcherite Tories, opposed to the soft wets
jack is a sailor, and AB (able-bodied seaman) is a sailor too

explanation.surface: A man named Jack is one of the hard-liners supporting a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dries is the British label for hard-line monetarist Conservatives of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird such as a gull or gannet flies, so it is fairly called a flier.

clue.text: Monsieur leaves museum a legacy

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the Monsieur letter departs from the museum

parts.note: the Hermitage is the great art museum in St Petersburg
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman bequeaths something to a museum in his will.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves wants to mean bequeaths, but it means departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is handed down from earlier generations, which is what a legacy is.

clue.text: A very handsome youth — and so I flourished

indicators.note: to flourish is to wave about with a showy gesture, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boast: I was a good-looking young man, and so I prospered.
explanation.walkthrough: Flourished reads as thrived, but it means brandished.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Adonis was a youth loved by Aphrodite, and his name is used for any strikingly good-looking young man.
